title: Align execution with LangGraph built-in capabilities
objective: Refactor langgraph-exec so its YAML compiler and application-specific policy layer use LangGraph's tested runtime capabilities instead of duplicating graph scheduling, looping, retry, timeout, fan-out, fan-in, and execution observability behavior.

branch.name: wi-0005-langgraph-builtins
branch.rationale: The work changes execution architecture and runtime API boundaries while preserving the YAML DSL and provider contracts.

request.text: Write a new .docs/work-items/* to address the LangGraph built-in feature alignment review: remove duplicated runtime behavior where applicable and lean on built-in, well-tested LangGraph components.

scope.name: native-graph-lowering
scope.description: Lower bounded loops, static parallel branches, dynamic maps, joins, and switch routing into StateGraph cycles, edges, conditional edges, Send, and reducer channels where semantics match.
scope.reason: LangGraph should own graph scheduling and state transition semantics rather than a parallel custom execution runtime.

scope.name: native-runtime-policies
scope.description: Map operational retry and timeout configuration to LangGraph node policies while retaining provider-specific structured response handling where required.
scope.reason: LangGraph provides tested retry classification, backoff, timeout, and task execution behavior.

scope.name: runtime-observability
scope.description: Replace inaccurate precomputed graph debug events with LangGraph stream/task/debug updates and preserve only accurate DSL-specific projections.
scope.reason: Execution diagnostics must describe actual node inputs, outputs, routes, and failures.

scope.name: runtime-api-boundary
scope.description: Preserve the current invoke contract while designing an optional runtime forwarding boundary for stream and future checkpointer support without claiming persistence.
scope.reason: The current wrapper hides useful LangGraph runtime capabilities and makes future persistence/resume adoption require another redesign.

scope.name: compatibility-and-tests
scope.description: Document semantic differences, preserve public-port and bounded-budget behavior, add provider-free regression coverage, and verify the package release gates.
scope.reason: Replacing custom orchestration can change failure, ordering, retry, timeout, and inspection behavior unless explicitly tested.

nonGoals.name: dsl-replacement
nonGoals.description: Do not remove YAML schemas, trusted imports, digest checks, public ports, nested-component encapsulation, or registered implementation restrictions.
nonGoals.reason: These are application-specific compiler and trust-boundary responsibilities that LangGraph does not provide.

nonGoals.name: persistence-and-human-control
nonGoals.description: Do not implement checkpoint persistence, interrupt/resume, Command-based human approval, or durable side-effect receipts in this work item.
nonGoals.reason: Those capabilities require a separate persistence and human-control contract with replay and side-effect evidence.

nonGoals.name: live-provider-release
nonGoals.description: Do not require authenticated live provider calls or production deployment evidence.
nonGoals.reason: Fake components and injected completion services provide deterministic evidence for this refactor.

items.name: preserve-dsl-boundary
items.description: The refactor must preserve YAML validation, trusted imports, public ports, nested-component encapsulation, registered implementations, and the llm provider boundary.
items.reason: LangGraph runtime adoption must not remove application-specific trust and composition guarantees.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Existing node, graph, nested-component, import-security, and provider-free validation tests continue to pass, or any intentional contract change has an explicit schema/version migration and regression test.

items.name: native-control-flow
items.description: Graph loops, static parallel branches, dynamic maps, joins, and switch routes must use LangGraph graph primitives rather than separate runtime traversal where applicable.
items.reason: LangGraph should own scheduling, supersteps, conditional transitions, fan-out, and reducer-based aggregation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Provider-free tests demonstrate bounded loop cycles, static fan-out/fan-in, dynamic map work, reducer joins, and conditional routing through a compiled StateGraph.

items.name: native-operational-policies
items.description: Operational node retry and timeout behavior must use LangGraph retryPolicy and timeout facilities when their semantics match the repository contract.
items.reason: The built-in policies provide standardized retry classification, backoff, timeout errors, and runtime integration.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tests prove finite retry attempts, retry classification, timeout behavior, and no late state update, while provider-specific structured response retries remain at the correct provider boundary.

items.name: accurate-observability
items.description: Execution diagnostics must be derived from actual LangGraph runtime events rather than precomputed inputs or final-state projections.
items.reason: Debug output is part of the operational contract and must not report inaccurate node data.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tests show that node, route, update, task, and public-port diagnostics correspond to the actual execution order and values.

items.name: bounded-runtime-api
items.description: The compiled runtime boundary must preserve invoke behavior and define a safe path for LangGraph stream/runtime options without falsely claiming persistence or resume.
items.reason: Callers should not be forced through a wrapper that discards useful built-in runtime capabilities.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The public API documents the supported invoke/stream surface, preserves current CLI behavior, and explicitly reports persistence and interrupt/resume as unavailable until a later work item.

items.name: release-evidence
items.description: The refactor must have deterministic test, typecheck, build, diff, and local CLI evidence with explicit limitations.
items.reason: The change affects execution architecture and requires evidence beyond isolated helper tests.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The complete provider-free suite, typecheck, build, CLI smoke checks, and repository diff checks pass, with no claim of live provider, persistence, or production readiness.
